method: clinical ocular biometry of live eagle owls (optical biometric device named for the axial length; orbital ultrasonography also used for segment measures)
conditions: 12 healthy eyes (6 right, 6 left) of 6 owls brought to Kafkas University (Kars, Turkiye) facilities, the Wildlife Conservation and Rehabilitation Center and the Veterinary Faculty Animal Hospital, for non-ocular problems; birds judged adult from wing structure and body size, sex estimated from body size only; no sedation or anaesthesia for the measurements. The sentence quoted is in the Discussion and gives the range; the Abstract gives AGL 31.108±0.1773 mm and the Results give a total mean of 31.10 mm (SEM 0.17) over the 12 eyes. The Discussion also says the axial lengths are similar to those of the Snowy owl. Birds with a history of trauma, prolonged malnutrition or poor general condition were excluded.

source.authors: Ermutlu CŞ, Balyen L, Özaydın İ, Kılıç E, Aksoy Ö, Büyükbaki HG, Büyükbaki B, Aydın U, Yıldız U, Ermutlu DG
source.title: Anterior and Posterior Segment Parameters of the Eye in Eagle Owls (Bubo bubo)

quote: Eye axial lengths of eagle owls, were measured between 30.9 mm and 31.35 mm.
note: New trait: eye_axial_length_mm (axial length of the globe, not an equatorial diameter; the key eye_diameter_mm is not used because the paper measures axial length). Whole sentence, one tool piece, printed with the comma after 'owls'. The page prints no family and no class for the species; order Strigiformes and class Aves are taken from the paper's reference titles ('Aves: Strigiformes'), the text itself says only 'the owl family' and 'Raptors family', so family is left blank. Licence: page prints Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial 4.0 International (CC BY-NC 4.0); Crossref gives no licence, no volume or issue, issue year 2023 and the title without '(Bubo bubo)', so printed year 2024 (running header 'Kafkas Univ Vet Fak Derg 30 (1): 81-86, 2024') and the page title are followed. Page byline in capitals with Turkish diacritics (Büyükbaki is printed BÜYÜKBAKİ in capitals). Not a mean: the sentence gives a range only.

method: taxonomic description of preserved type specimens
conditions: Species-level statement in the generic assignment of a new species. Type series: holotype adult female IAvH-Am-15487 (Colombia, Santander, El Carmen de Chucuri, vereda La Belleza, Cascajales River, 789 m) and four paratypes (2 adult females, 2 adult males); two juveniles are referred, non-type specimens. Description of the holotype: 'Eyes visible but small, eye diameter 4% of head length and 13.5% of eye-nostril distance'; Variation of type series: eye diameter 4-8% of head length and 10-19% of eye-nostril distance (Table 3 lists eye diameter 0.2-0.4 mm); eyeballs completely violet blue in life. The Discussion cites orbit (open versus closed) evidence used by Wilkinson et al. (2013) for Parvicaecilia and Microcaecilia and says the authors consider their own evidence insufficient to settle it. The Diagnosis has no eye wording.

source.authors: Acosta-Galvis AR, Torres M, Pulido-Santacruz P
source.title: A new species of Caecilia (Gymnophiona, Caeciliidae) from the Magdalena valley region of Colombia

where: Description of new species, Generic assignment
quote: The new species is assignable to the genus Caecilia because its eyes are not covered by bone and it has tentacles below the nostrils (Type D sensu Lynch, 1999, Fig. 3 D–E).
note: Whole sentence, 29 words, reassembled from two consecutive tool pieces (the join falls at the space after 'tentacles'); another desk unit dropped this sentence as 'arrived in pieces', the join here is at an ordinary space of one printed sentence. The page-top title omits the subtitle that the citation line carries (', with comments on the genus Parvicaecilia', and a colon after Gymnophiona); Crossref gives the page-top form and the page-top form is filed. Higher taxa: no Class, Order or Family heading; Gymnophiona and Caeciliidae from the title, Amphibia from the keywords. Licence: page prints the Creative Commons Attribution License (CC BY 4.0) sentence; Crossref CC BY 4.0 vor. Volume 884, no issue.

value: none: workers without compound eyes and ocelli
eye: compound eyes and ocelli, worker caste
conditions: Worker caste only. Holotype worker GXU220610-W-01 and five paratype workers (W-02 to W-06) from one colony at Qianjiang village, Yuemiao Mountain, Haining, Zhejiang, China, collected 10 June 2022. The single dealate queen (N = 1, a non-type specimen from the same colony) has eyes: the Queen description says 'compound eyes present approximately at mid-length of the head side' and 'ocelli present and closely approximated (Fig. 3A)'. The male is unknown. The Recognition section restates 'eyes absent in the worker caste'.

note: Whole short sentence in the worker Head description; it does not name the species or caste, the section heading does. Described as new in this paper. Page byline and Crossref list the same seven authors in the same order. Volume 1205, no issue. The Zenodo copy of the treatment is CC0 and was not used.

value: male imago: compound eyes contiguous; upper portion brown, lower portion black
conditions: Male imago (in ethanol) description, whose holotype is a male imago with final nymphal exuviae from China, Yunnan, Dali, Jianchuan County, Jinlong River, 2371 m, 9 May 2022; paratypes are 40 nymphs, 24 imagos and 20 subimagos reared from nymphs of the same site and date. The female imago and nymph descriptions carry no eye wording, and the Diagnosis does not mention eyes. The sentence does not mention turbinate eyes or ocelli.
